IN THIS PROJECTThe problemThe approachSource evidenceLimitations & next steps
01 / CONTEXT

The problem.

Statistical functions can feel like a black box when learning hypothesis testing. Showing intermediate quantities beside a library result creates a useful starting point for understanding and checking the calculation.

02 / IMPLEMENTATION

The approach.

Accept two comma-separated samples, calculate summary quantities and a test statistic, then display a SciPy independent-samples test result alongside the manual calculation.

01Two numeric samples
02Manual calculation + SciPy
03Displayed test outputs
01

Simple sample input

Enter two numeric samples through a Streamlit interface and choose a hypothesis direction.

02

Intermediate calculations

The source displays a manual t statistic, degrees of freedom, and a p-value, making the implementation inspectable.

03

A library comparison

The code calls SciPy with equal_var=False. Comparing both paths exposes why assumptions and degrees of freedom must agree.

04 / REFLECTION & NEXT STEPS

What I’d improve next.

  • The manual path combines an unequal-variance standard error with pooled degrees of freedom; it needs correction to match Welch’s test.
  • The one-sided labels must be mapped to SciPy’s supported alternatives before those options work correctly.
  • Normality diagnostics, variance diagnostics, and confidence intervals are not implemented in the reviewed source.
NEXT ITERATION

Correct the statistical paths, add input validation and reference tests, and explain assumptions before extending the interface.

For statistical software, correctness and transparent assumptions are part of the product experience.
